items.justification: Uniqueness of device security parameters versus security testing before release.
Management of critical security parameters versus guidance on appropriate use and failure modes.
Both remove access that is not needed for operation, A by disabling unused interfaces, B by limiting the permissions the system holds elsewhere.
Limiting unauthenticated disclosure over network interfaces versus documenting training data provenance.
Secure boot verification versus the permissions an AI system holds on other systems.
Lifecycle management of security parameters versus the assessment preceding a decision to build.
Presence of a secure update mechanism versus involving Data Custodians in requirements discussions.
Publishing a disclosure route and supporting users through an incident are separate obligations under one external incident-handling capability.
Physical protection of debug ports versus contractual terms with cloud providers.
Orderly network reconnection versus monitoring model behaviour for security-relevant drift.
Secure development process versus communicating unresolvable threats down the supply chain.
Secure boot verifies the software at runtime and supply chain process governs how it was built; together they assure software integrity.
Vulnerability rectification depends on knowing which assets and versions are deployed, which is what B mandates.
Both require accessible guidance to the end user on setting up and configuring the system securely.
Reviewed cryptographic implementations versus permissions granted on connected systems.
Secure development of one's own software versus re-evaluating third-party released models.
Vulnerability disclosure policy versus preview access that lets operators evaluate model changes.
Cryptography for secure communication versus the business case assessment preceding an AI system.
Both require independent competent review of the security implementation, A of the cryptographic implementation, B through independent testers.
Ease of applying an update versus the risk of unused model capability.
Validation of network input versus asset tracking and version control.
Informing the user that an update is needed versus technical measures supporting human oversight of a model.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus measures enabling human oversight.
Transit encryption versus an organizational review of access control frameworks; B does not reach data in transit.
Timeliness of security updates versus threat modelling on configuration change.
Both ensure users learn that a security update exists, A by the device checking, B by the operator notifying.
Verifying update authenticity versus selecting controls against corporate risk tolerance.
Both address products that cannot be updated; A mandates transparency and replacement support, B contingency mitigation of the residual risk.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus incident management and recovery planning.
Guidance on checking a secure state versus support offered during and after an incident.
Reviewed cryptographic implementations versus designed-in human oversight capability.
Code minimization versus the provision and delivery of security patches.
Validation of user interface input versus maintaining an audit trail over models and datasets.
Reviewed cryptographic implementations versus security update delivery.
Minimizing security decisions asked of the user and explaining security updates clearly are different obligations serving usable security.
Both contain a compromise by enforced isolation, A between memory regions, B between development and production environments.
Secure development processes versus contingency planning where updates cannot be provided.
Code minimization versus assurance that an external risk owner can address its risks.
Disabling unused interfaces reduces attack surface; B concerns confidentiality of training and test data.
Disabling debug interfaces versus accessible user guidance on system configuration.
